deadline.value: Fall 2027 Priority Deadline is December 1, 2026 (final deadline March 15, 2027); admits once a year for Fall only.
deadline.quote: Integrated Biomedical Sciences (PhD) | School of Medicine | Doctoral | Priority Deadline: December 1, 2026 | Deadline: March 15, 2027

also.quote: Students will be admitted once a year on a full-time basis, with coursework beginning in the fall semester.

gre_general.value: GRE General scores taken within the past five years are required (competitive applicants >300 overall and >150 quantitative).
gre_general.quote: Submission of satisfactory Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores taken within the past five years.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Biomedical Sciences; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Pre-admission supervisor agreement is not required; students complete 8 credit hours of lab rotations during the first year and declare a lab in May.
supervisor.quote: Because we accept only a handful of candidates, everyone gets to know you, and through rotations with different faculty, you’ll find an advisor who will mentor you and help you find and pursue your research passion.

funding.value: All accepted students receive a $32,000/year graduate assistantship including health benefits plus full tuition sponsorship (program sponsors Year 1; research advisor sponsors thereafter).
funding.quote: All accepted students are awarded an assistantship of $32,000 per year, including health benefits. Tuition is also covered by a sponsor.

also.quote: Each student admitted into the IBMS program receives a graduate stipend in the amount of $32,000 per year plus benefits.

entry_route.value: Requires a baccalaureate degree in a related field, minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale, and a B or higher in Biochemistry (97 credit hours total).
entry_route.quote: A baccalaureate degree in a related field from a college or university recognized by a national accrediting body.

notes: 97-credit-hour Ph.D. in Integrated Biomedical Sciences (IBMS) with areas of expertise in Cellular and Molecular Biology, Immunology and Infectious Diseases, and Pulmonary Physiology. Requires 3 letters of recommendation, CV/resume, personal statement naming up to 3 faculty of interest, GRE > 300 (>150 quantitative competitive), GPA >= 3.0, and grade B or higher in Biochemistry.
name: Integrated Biomedical Sciences Ph.D.
